title: Cliff Jackson and Duke Ellington in Washington
summary: They discuss their relationship as young Washington musicians; Cliff did not claim discovering Duke.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: First of all, was there a relationship between him and Duke Ellington, you know, during the time that he lived in Washington, because they both must have come to New York about the same time?

I'm not sure if they both came to New York about the same time, but it was certainly right around -- within a few years. But of course all the musicians knew each other down there around Washington, D.C. Elmer Snowden
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

takes credit for having discovered Duke Ellington. But Cliff identified more with James P. Johnson and Fats Waller, he was crazy about both of them. I think that they shared a lot of interests among them.
